To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fish oil supplementation increases the proportion of EPA and DHA in the myocardium and that this effect is not dependent on the dose of fish oil or the duration of supplementation.

fish oil supplementation does not affect serum lipids in patients with hypercholesterolemia, does not improve endothelium-dependent vasodilation in patients with coronary disease, and does not affect the risk of death from coronary artery disease in healthy individuals.

the effects of fish oil on myocardial fatty acid composition were modest, and that there was no significant difference in the effects of fish-oil supplements on myocardial fatty-acid content in patients with and without a history of myocardial infarction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary supplementation with fish oil, rich in omega 3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA) on myocardial fatty acid composition.
the effect of dietary fish oil supplementation on myocardial lipid composition.
the effect of fish oil on myocardial fatty acid composition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fish oil supplementation does not improve cardiovascular risk factors and does not improve clinical outcomes.

fish oil supplementation does not appear to have a significant effect on myocardial triglyceride levels, although it does increase the amount of omega-3 fatty acids in myocardial membranes and decrease the proportion of saturated fatty acids.

fish oil is effective in reducing the incidence of cardiovascular disease in the general population and in secondary prevention in patients who have already experienced a cardiovascular event, and it is safe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of fish oil supplementation on the myocardium of patients with coronary disease are not clear, and there is no evidence that fish oil supplementation is associated with any benefit on myocardial fatty acid content.

we have been able to demonstrate that the consumption of fish oil in a dose of about 1.8 g of EPA and DHA daily for 6 months has a significant effect on myocardial fatty acid composition in patients with stable coronary heart disease, and that this effect is associated with a significant improvement in myocardial function.
the effects of fish-oil on myocardial triglycerides and fatty acids in humans are variable, and that these effects are not necessarily linked to the changes in the blood.

we can use the power of the gut microbiome to help prevent the onset of cardiovascular diseases, which is the leading cause of death in the U.S. and the world.
